author: f. e. wilson
title: Stockton Nursing Center held 1-star CMS rating in San Joaquin County during Q1
text:
Stockton Nursing Center was under the ownership of Sapphire Operations, LLC in the first quarter of 2026, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) reports. The San Joaquin County nursing home has been owned by Sapphire Operations, LLC since Sep. 1, 2024.
The facility is classified as for-profit.
In that time frame, Stockton Nursing Center earned an overall CMS rating of one, falling below California’s average for nursing homes, which stands at 3.2. CMS assigns ratings based on factors including health inspection results, staffing, and the quality of care provided.
CMS data shows the center cared for an average of 112.9 residents daily in the first quarter of 2026 and operated with 119 available beds. The center is currently not affiliated with a hospital.
During this time period, Stockton Nursing Center incurred a total of $83,719 in fines across five incidents and received five penalties.
There were 22 for-profit nursing homes operating in San Joaquin County, California, in total.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates show the national population of older adults continues to increase amid declining numbers in younger age brackets. Between 2020 and 2024, the count of Americans aged 65 and older rose by 13%, while the population under 18 decreased by 1.7%. The older adult population has expanded significantly over the past 100 years, growing from 4.9 million in 1920 to over 61 million in 2024.
A 2021 study found that almost half of people in this age group, about 28 million, may eventually require long-term services and supports. The study also forecasts that more than one-third may need nursing home care at some point.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome, executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance, an insurance education group. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
